facts.text: Cherokee Village was founded by John Cooper Sr. in 1948, who bought 400 acres along the South Fork River to create a family summer retreat.
The community grew as Cooper purchased an additional 2,400 acres, carving out lots and building lakes, leading to the first planned recreation community in Arkansas.
Cherokee Village was dedicated in June 1955 with one lake and an airstrip, marking the start of its planned development.
In 1998 the Sharp County portion was annexed, uniting the entire area into a single city that now spans over 13,000 acres.
Cherokee Village boasts seven lakes and two marinas, with Lake Thunderbird being the largest, offering more than seven miles of shoreline.
After Cherokee Village became a city, the Cherokee Village School District and CVSID split duties, with CVSID preserving parks, golf courses, and lakes.
